attributes.action: Increase the DWP Christmas Bonus Amount which has remained at £10 since 1972
attributes.additional_details: The scheme was introduced by the UK government in 1972 and has been awarded ever since to those who claim certain benefits. When it was originally introduced under the Pensioners and Family Income Supplement Payments Act £10 would stretch quite some way being roughly equivalent to £171 in 2026. However this "bonus" has remained exactly the same amount for 54 years while  costs have risen steadily. In 1972 a pint of milk was 5p, 2026; 72p. £10 isn't a bonus it's an insult.
attributes.background: Increase the DWP Christmas bonus in line with inflation or to at least £100 as £10 is virtually worthless today in comparison to it's value in 1972.

rejection.details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/784268
